findings.reason: a worker deriving the baseline from the only per-name record labelled "names that name the operator" would take 71/25/8 and exempt the omitted names, so both the baseline and the final count would silently exempt the six names the pass exists to repair, and the declared negative control could not fire.
findings.text: §6's population "(the names that name the operator …)" fits two different sets in the cited record, and the one its wording matches is self-exempting: `rewrite-closing-census.json` records `operators.<op>.name_count` over names whose id carries the operator (flux_surface_averaged 73, line_averaged 28, time_derivative 9) and `operator_phrases.<op>.names_naming_the_operator` over names whose *definition* names the operator (71, 25, 8), with the 2, 3 and 1 excluded names all sitting in `<omitted>` — precisely the names that never state the operator. A count taken over the second population drops those names instead of reporting them as not carrying the stored sentence, so the measure can reach "none" while definitions still never name the operator, and the last bullet's planted control — "an operator name planted there stating no form of its operator" — falls outside the population and cannot be reported at all; the first bullet's "every live name that names the operator" already reads as the name-carries-the-operator set, so the parenthetical contradicts it
